prompt.context: Our client is TNT Funds, a small asset management firm. TNT Funds manages investments in mutual funds from wealthy individuals. Their account portfolio varies in the average account balance and in the range of financial assets invested. TNT Funds' revenues derive from a fixed annual management fee for their accounts. TNT Funds is owned by a parent company, an insurance company. The firm has 2 main sales channels: an online platform, by which clients can buy and sell mutual funds, and direct sales through agents of the parent company. TNT Funds reported losses during the last 2 years and its future projections are not bright either.
prompt.question: TNT Funds has hired McKinsey to determine why they are not profitable and what they can do to turn around their current position.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current average account balance?
What is the total value of funds managed?
What is the variable cost per account?
What is the management fee rate?
How many insurance customers does the parent company have?
clarifying_info.a: 4 million, and this number will remain constant

clarifying_info.q: What is the current mutual funds industry volume?
What will the average balance of insurance customer accounts be in 5 years?

framework: Decreasing Revenues: Internal Factors — efficiency of sales channels, incentives, methodology, pricing
Decreasing Revenues: External Factors — customer trends, competition (rivals and substitutes)
Increasing Costs: Overhead — IT investments, increase in headcount, office/administration costs
Increasing Costs: Sales Channels — commissions, transaction costs

questions.prompt: TNT Funds would like to generate more revenue to balance their fixed overhead costs. By how much should they aim to increase the average account balance of their clients in order to achieve a 10% profit margin?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first compute total number of accounts, then allocated fixed cost per account, total cost per account, required revenue per account at 10% margin, and back into the required account balance.

math.setup: Total accounts = Total funds managed / Average account balance. Allocated fixed cost per account = Total fixed costs / Total accounts. Total cost per account = variable cost + allocated fixed cost. For 10% margin: Revenue per account = Total cost per account / (1 - 0.10). Required average account balance = Revenue per account / management fee rate.
steps: Increase needed = $6,100 - $5,000 = $1,100, which is a 22% growth
math.answer: Average account balance must grow by $1,100 (22%) from $5,000 to $6,100.

questions.prompt: In the mutual fund industry, most firms operate only one sales channel — either indirect (call center, online) or direct (agents). Why would you think that is the case?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify two dimensions: (1) customer segment fit — high-balance investors want personalized service while small investors want quick self-service access; (2) capability and cost structure — indirect channels require strong IT/operations (high fixed, low marginal cost) while direct channels require deep product expertise (low fixed, high management cost). Running both simultaneously creates cost and focus inefficiencies without scale.

questions.prompt: Now, assume TNT was to focus on the direct sales channel to grow their customer base. What percentage of the insurance clients will they need to capture in 5 years if they wanted to manage 1% of the mutual funds industry volume?
questions.guidance: Candidate must project the mutual fund industry volume forward 5 years at 10% CAGR, compute 1% of that volume as the target AUM, divide by the projected average account balance to get required number of customers, and express as a percentage of total insurance customers.

math.setup: Industry volume in year 5 = $1T × (1.10)^5. Target AUM = 1% of year-5 volume. Required customers = Target AUM / average account balance per customer. Capture rate = Required customers / total insurance customers.
math.answer: TNT Funds would need to capture 40% of the parent company's 4 million insurance clients.

brainstorming.prompt: Why do most mutual fund firms operate only one sales channel?

categories.name: Customer Segmentation
ideas: High-balance investors require personalized, relationship-driven service best served by direct agents
Small investors prioritize speed and self-service access, well served by online/indirect channels
Each segment has different price sensitivity and product complexity needs

categories.name: Company Capabilities and Cost Structure
ideas: Indirect channel requires strong IT infrastructure and efficient operations (high fixed cost, low marginal cost)
Direct channel requires deep mutual fund expertise and relationship management (low fixed cost, high variable/management cost)
Building and maintaining both sets of capabilities simultaneously is costly and difficult for small firms

categories.name: Strategic Focus
ideas: Splitting effort across two channels dilutes management attention and brand positioning
Economies of scale are harder to achieve when fixed costs are spread across two channels
A small firm like TNT struggles to amortize fixed costs without sufficient volume in each channel

recommendation: TNT Funds should pivot to focus exclusively on the direct sales channel through the parent insurance company's agent network, and divest or wind down the indirect online platform.
By concentrating on direct sales, TNT can leverage the parent company's 4 million existing customer relationships, targeting high-balance investors who generate more revenue per account.
risks: Capturing 40% of parent insurance customers in 5 years is an aggressive target that depends on agent training quality and incentive alignment
Revenue from indirect channel will be lost during transition, potentially deepening near-term losses
Insurance agents may lack the mutual fund expertise needed to serve high-end customers without significant training investment
next_steps: Train parent company insurance agents on mutual fund products to ensure they can serve high-end customers effectively
Review and redesign agent incentive structure to align with TNT Funds growth targets
Develop a plan to wind down indirect channel operations and reallocate associated fixed costs
Set milestone-based targets for customer capture rate (e.g., 10% at year 1, 25% at year 3, 40% at year 5)
